findings.issue: The ceiling's expect label hard-codes the word 'half' ('leaves the table at least half the screen it is read on') while the bound it judges is STACK_CEILING_SHARE, a named constant printed two words later. Change the constant to 0.4 and the line still says 'half' while printing '= 0.4 of 844px', so the label's claim and its own basis would disagree.
findings.resolution: Derive the wording from the constant, for example 'leaves the table at least ${1 - STACK_CEILING_SHARE} of the screen it is read on', or drop the fraction word and keep only the printed '<px> ceiling = <share> of <height>px' basis.

intent.note: R6 clause 'keep the layer-derived bound and the single stackOverTable() measurement': kept. stackOverTable() is unchanged and still the only measurement. judgeStack()'s first expect computes the same bound (sum of layers + STACK_SLACK_PX) and produces a label byte-identical to the old one for both halves. I checked this by expanding the template: `ph1 ${what}, ${where}, pins no more than the ${layers.long joined ' and the '}` gives 'pins no more than the strip and the shut filter bar' for the shut half and 'the strip' for the open half. Clause 'On the same shutStack result, add a ceiling: a share of PHONE_TALL with its basis stated in a comment': `const STACK_CEILING_SHARE = 0.5; const STACK_CEILING_PX = Math.floor(PHONE_TALL.height * STACK_CEILING_SHARE)`, with the basis comment 'the table keeps at least half of the screen it is read on', judged as `m.stack <= STACK_CEILING_PX` on shutStack. The diff also applies the ceiling to openStack, which the clause does not ask for. It is the same class (the strip-only bound grows with the strip), so this is a justified widening rather than a divergence. Clause 'Prove it red by inflating .sectools' height in a scratch copy of the acme report': the claim reports this by hand (.sectools{min-height:600px}: layer line ok at 648/650.4, ceiling FAIL at 648/422, exit 1). I did not re-run it; my role allows no gate or browser run and testsAdded is empty. R7 clauses: the layout-baseline.mjs header now states the new arm ('one hit-test down the middle of the screen, taken with More filters shut and, on a report that has the panel, again open. Each result is judged twice — against the layers that state allows ... and against a ceiling'). The 'saturates' and 'shut figure has NO absolute bar' paragraphs are replaced. Both notes at judge() now say '(the absolute stack check above did, against its layers and its ceiling)'. That holds because the shut half runs outside the More-filters branch before judge() at line 2709; the only exceptions are paths that already push a FAIL (bar already open, or stack unmeasured). 'No F/P/BUG ids in comments': none were added. The claim describes the diff: byte-identical layer labels, both call sites, the CONTRIBUTING.md:526-528 rewrite (named as an undeclared path), the reworded relative failure message that keeps /separate line above/ for the test at layout-baseline.test.mjs:157, and the remaining 'absolute bar' comments in the test file (137/151/241), which I read as still true. The stamp grades 'current' under stamp-verification.py compare (exit 0). The claim's figures (acme 279/49 px, demo-large 337 px, the red probes) come from runs I did not repeat.
